en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Confession (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Bhojanavagga 40.
The Training Rule on Tooth-sticks:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Forest, in the Gabled Hall.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhu who was a strict wearer of refuse-rags (sabbapaṃsukūlika) was dwelling in a charnel ground.
He did not wish to accept what was being given by people; rather, he himself took discarded items from the charnel ground, or from the foot of a tree, or from a threshold, and used them.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can this monk take for himself and consume these items stolen from our noble sirs?
This elder monk is a glutton; he must be eating human flesh!
The monks heard those people grumbling, complaining, and spreading their grievances.
Those monks who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about:
"How can a monk take food that has not been given into the opening of his mouth?"... [They asked:
"Is it true, monk, that you take food that has not been given into the opening of your mouth?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“… How can you, foolish man, consume food that has not been given through the gateway of the mouth?”
“Monk, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:
‘If any monk should take food into his mouth that has not been given, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).’”
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.
Now at that time, the monks were anxious about using water as a tooth-cleanser.
They reported this matter to the Blessed One... [as before] ...
“I allow you, monks, to take up a tooth-stick with water and use it.
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule:
‘Whatever monk should put into his mouth food that has not been given, except for water and a tooth-stick, there is an offense of expiation.’”
"But whoever" means whoever such a person...
"a monk."
...pe... this is the meaning intended here by "bhikkhu.
"Not given" (adinnam) means that which has not been received.

"Given" means that when one gives with the body, or with what is connected to the body, or with something relinquishable, and [the recipient] receives it with the body or with what is connected to the body while standing within arm's reach, this is called "given.
"Food" means:
With the exception of water and tooth-cleansing sticks, whatever is swallowed is called "nutriment.
"Except for water and tooth-cleansing sticks" means excluding water and tooth-cleansing sticks.
If one takes [food] thinking, “I will eat it; I will consume it,” there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For every mouthful swallowed, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one consumes food from the mouth when it has not been formally received, perceiving it as not having been formally received, except for water and tooth-wood, there is an offense of expiation.
If one eats food at the mouth-door that has not been received, being in doubt about it—except for water and tooth-wood—one commits an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one eats food at the mouth-door that has not been received, perceiving it as having been received—except for water and tooth-wood—one commits an offense of expiation.
If one eats food at the mouth-door that has been received, perceiving it as not having been received, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it has been accepted and he is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it has been accepted and he perceives that it has been accepted, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
If, when there is water for rinsing the teeth and the four kinds of raw flesh, one takes them oneself and consumes them when there is a reason to do so but no one is available to make them allowable,
except in the case of one who is insane.
"For the first offender":
the tenth training rule on tooth-sticks is concluded.
The fourth chapter on food is finished.
Its summary verse:
Alms-food, a group, another, and cake;
and two types of invitation are mentioned.
At the wrong time, storing up milk,
and you bite with a tooth-stick.
